text: {"features":[{"evidence":"\"Master's degree\" or \"Doctoral degree\" in computer science","name":"Degree level","description":"This captures the highest relevant academic credential the letter presents, which varies from meeting the minimum with a bachelor's degree to matching the preference for graduate study.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relevant bachelor's degree or equivalent only."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Relevant master's degree."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Relevant doctoral degree."}]},{"evidence":"\"7 years ... testing, maintaining, and launching 6 production services\"","name":"Production track record","description":"This captures how much credible evidence the letter gives of sustained ownership of real production software through build, launch, maintenance, and operations.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Minimal or thinly described production experience, with little sense of scope or ownership."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Meets the baseline with some production work, but the footprint or maturity looks modest."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows solid multi-year production experience across several services with clear backend relevance."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows extensive and mature production ownership across multiple services, with strong signals of sustained operational responsibility."}]},{"evidence":"\"automated vulnerability triage workflows\"","name":"Security triage automation","description":"This captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, or prioritization.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No evidence of vulnerability-handling automation."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security automation in general terms, but not a clear vulnerability-triage example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes concrete ownership of tooling that automated vulnerability intake or triage."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows end-to-end triage automation with specific functions such as classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or explicit reduction of manual work."}]},{"evidence":"\"Python agents ... Go services define permissions and audit their actions\"","name":"Agentic tooling design","description":"This captures whether the letter shows experience architecting agentic systems in which AI agents act within deliberately engineered boundaries.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No agentic tooling example is given."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions agents or agentic systems, but without much architecture or control detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a concrete agentic design, typically pairing Python agents with Go backends or similar components."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explains deliberate agent architecture with meaningful detail about autonomy, permissions, auditability, task decomposition, or guardrails."}]},{"evidence":"\"LLM-backed features\" and \"evaluation scaffolding\"","name":"Applied AI reliability","description":"This captures how convincingly the letter shows production AI experience with attention to evaluation, trustworthiness, and failure modes rather than simple AI enthusiasm.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No meaningful AI experience is presented."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI or LLM exposure, but without production responsibility or reliability detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows hands-on production AI work and at least some awareness of evaluation or failure modes."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Demonstrates substantial AI delivery with explicit safeguards, evaluation practices, or nuanced discussion of trustworthiness in production."}]},{"evidence":"\"threat models and follow-through\"","name":"Security assessment practice","description":"This captures hands-on experience assessing systems through threat modeling, reviews, attack-surface analysis, findings, and remediation follow-through.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No evidence of security assessment work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Signals security interest or knowledge, but not concrete assessment practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes real assessments such as threat models, code review, service reviews, or findings verification."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents security assessment as a recurring engineering discipline with concrete methods and remediation ownership."}]},{"evidence":"\"Python became my workhorse\"","name":"Python depth","description":"This captures how strongly the letter establishes Python as a real implementation language for services, tooling, automation, or analysis.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No Python evidence, or only an implied familiarity."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Python as a language used, but with little depth or ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular Python use for tooling, automation, services, or prototypes."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Establishes production-grade Python ownership, such as typed or tested services, internal platforms, or pervasive operational use."}]},{"evidence":"\"turned a brute-force correlation job into a streaming computation\"","name":"Algorithmic fluency","description":"This captures demonstrated command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering improvements rather than generic claims.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No algorithmic evidence is given."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims strong algorithms knowledge, but offers little supporting detail."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives a concrete example of an algorithmic redesign or better structure choice improving a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Repeatedly or vividly demonstrates algorithmic judgment on meaningful performance, scaling, or correctness problems."}]},{"evidence":"\"foundational infrastructure\" and \"strengthening the development lifecycle\"","name":"Foundational security motivation","description":"This captures how clearly the letter explains why platform-level security engineering, rather than generic software work, is the applicant's intended direction.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Expresses generic interest in the role with little reason tied to foundational security work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows some interest in security or scale, but the motivation remains broad."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly wants platform or lifecycle security work and explains why it fits the applicant's trajectory."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents a strong, specific, and credible motivation for central security infrastructure as a deliberate career choice."}]},{"evidence":"\"variant analysis\" and \"scale scarce security judgment\"","name":"Role-specific insight","description":"This captures how well the letter shows understanding of this team's actual charter, leverage points, and technical shape.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Reads as largely generic and could fit many software or security roles."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions one or two role-relevant ideas, but only at a high level."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows clear understanding of developer-facing security automation and the team's leverage."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Demonstrates nuanced grasp of this exact role, using details like variant analysis, incoming vulnerability handling, expert-capacity scaling, or the Go-backend and Python-agent split."}]},{"evidence":"\"helping busy developer teams do the secure thing by default\"","name":"Developer-centered security mindset","description":"This captures whether the letter frames security tooling as something that reduces friction and helps developers adopt secure behavior by default.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows little sign of thinking about the downstream users of security tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions helping other engineers, but only in generic terms."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Clearly emphasizes secure defaults, reduced toil, or proactive assistance to developer teams."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Repeatedly centers usability, workflow fit, and the return of scarce expert attention as the point of the tooling."}]},{"evidence":"\"OSCP certification\" or \"CompTIA Security+\"","name":"Certification rigor","description":"This captures the strength of formal security credentialing the letter presents, from baseline knowledge signals to hands-on practical validation.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No security certification is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ that signals formalized fundamentals."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions a hands-on credential such as OSCP that signals practical offensive capability."}]},{"evidence":"\"capture-the-flag competitions\"","name":"CTF engagement","description":"This captures whether the letter shows ongoing adversarial practice through capture-the-flag participation and how serious that practice appears.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No CTF participation is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions casual or recurring CTF participation as skill maintenance."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows serious CTF engagement, such as frequent competition or near-top placements in strong fields."}]},{"evidence":"\"send patches upstream\" and \"maintain an open-source project\"","name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"This captures engagement with open-source software as a contributor or maintainer, especially when framed as responsible engineering practice.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No open-source contribution is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional fixes or patches with limited scope."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows regular upstream contribution or maintenance of a small project."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows clear stewardship, such as maintaining an actively used project, handling reviews and releases, or repeatedly fixing dependencies upstream."}]},{"evidence":"\"distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics\"","name":"Personal engineering initiative","description":"This captures evidence of self-directed technical building outside formal job scope, especially when the work is ambitious or sustained.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"No side project or independent technical work is mentioned."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small personal project, but with limited technical depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a substantive side project or sustained independent engineering habit."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows ambitious self-directed engineering, often with distributed systems, failure handling, or production-like standards."}]},{"evidence":"\"measured its worth in the hours of expert attention it returned\"","name":"Evidence specificity","description":"This captures how concrete the letter is in backing claims with named systems, mechanisms, outcomes, or examples.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mostly generic assertions and self-descriptions, with little supporting detail."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Some concrete facts appear, but many claims remain unsupported."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Several claims are anchored in specific systems, redesigns, mechanisms, or operational outcomes."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"The letter consistently grounds strengths in crisp technical examples, concrete mechanics, and clear impact."}]},{"evidence":"frequent visible typos such as \"Hiirng,\" \"prduction,\" or \"gnireenignE\"","name":"Writing polish","description":"This captures the degree to which spelling, grammar, and wording errors distract from an otherwise credible and professional application.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Frequent errors materially undermine professionalism or readability."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Several noticeable errors or awkward phrases are present."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Minor errors appear, but the letter remains professional overall."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Clean, polished writing with little or no distracting error."}]}]}
